entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12384"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 11</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Hos.11.1-Hos.11.12">Ho 11:1-12</reference>. God's Former Benefits, and Israel's Ingratitude Resulting in Punishment, Yet Jehovah Promises Restoration at Last.</title> <div sID="gen22681" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="Hos.11.5">Ho 11:5</reference> shows this prophecy was uttered after the league made with Egypt (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.17.4">2Ki 17:4</reference>).<div eID="gen22681" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22682" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12384"/><hi type="bold">1. Israel ... called my son out of Egypt--</hi>Bengel translates, "From the time that he (Israel) was in Egypt, I called him My son," which the parallelism proves. So <reference osisRef="Hos.12.9">Ho 12:9</reference> and <reference osisRef="Hos.13.4">Ho 13:4</reference> use "from ... Egypt," for "from the time that thou didst sojourn in Egypt." <reference osisRef="Exod.4.22">Ex 4:22</reference> also shows that Israel was called by God, "My son," from the time of his Egyptian sojourn (<reference osisRef="Isa.43.1">Is 43:1</reference>). God is always said to have led or brought forth, not to have "called," Israel from Egypt. <reference osisRef="Matt.2.15">Mt 2:15</reference>, therefore, in quoting this prophecy (typically and primarily referring to Israel, antitypically and fully to Messiah), applies it to Jesus' sojourn in Egypt, not His return from it. Even from His infancy, partly spent in Egypt, God called Him His son. God included Messiah, and Israel for Messiah's sake, in one common love, and therefore in one common prophecy. Messiah's people and Himself are one, as the Head and the body. <reference osisRef="Isa.49.3">Is 49:3</reference> calls Him "Israel." The same general reason, danger of extinction, caused the infant Jesus, and Israel in its national infancy (compare <reference osisRef="Gen.42.1-Gen.43.34">Ge 42:1-43:34</reference>; 45:18; 46:3, 4; <reference osisRef="Ezek.16.4-Ezek.16.6">Eze 16:4-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.31.20">Jr 31:20</reference>) to sojourn in Egypt. So He, and His spiritual Israel, are already called "God's sons" while yet in the Egypt of the world. <div eID="gen22682" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12388"/><div sID="gen22690" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12388"/><hi type="bold">5. He shall not return into ... Egypt--</hi>namely, to seek help against Assyria (compare <reference osisRef="Hos.7.11">Ho 7:11</reference>), as Israel lately had done (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.17.4">2Ki 17:4</reference>), after having revolted from Assyria, to whom they had been tributary from the times of Menahem (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.15.19">2Ki 15:19</reference>). In a figurative sense, "he shall return to Egypt" (<reference osisRef="Hos.9.3">Ho 9:3</reference>), that is, to Egypt-like bondage; also many Jewish fugitives were literally to return to Egypt, when the Holy Land was to be in Assyrian and Chaldean hands.<div eID="gen22690" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22691" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Assyrian shall be his king--</hi>instead of having kings of their own, and Egypt as their auxiliary.<div eID="gen22691" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22692" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">because they refused to return--</hi>just retribution. They would not return (spiritually) to God, therefore they shall not return (corporally) to Egypt, the object of their desire. <div eID="gen22692" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12390"/><div sID="gen22696" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12390"/><hi type="bold">7. bent to backsliding--</hi>Not only do they backslide, and that too from Me, their "chief good," but they are bent upon it. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12392"/><div sID="gen22700" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12392"/><hi type="bold">9. I will not return to destroy Ephraim--</hi>that is, I will no more, as in past times, destroy Ephraim. The destruction primarily meant is probably that by Tiglath-pileser, who, as the Jewish king Ahaz' ally against Pekah of Israel and Rezin of Syria, deprived Israel of Gilead, Galilee, and Naphtali (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.15.29">2Ki 15:29</reference>). The ulterior reference is to the long dispersion hereafter, to be ended by God's covenant mercy restoring His people, not for their merits, but of His grace.<div eID="gen22700" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22701" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">God, ... not man--</hi>not dealing as man would, with implacable wrath under awful provocation (<reference osisRef="Isa.55.7-Isa.55.9">Is 55:7-9</reference>; Mal 3:6). I do not, like man, change when once I have made a covenant of everlasting love, as with Israel (<reference osisRef="Num.23.19">Nu 23:19</reference>). We measure God by the human standard, and hence are slow to credit fully His promises; these, however, belong to the faithful remnant, not to the obstinately impenitent.<div eID="gen22701" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22702" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in the midst of thee--</hi>as peculiarly thy God (<reference osisRef="Exod.19.5">Ex 19:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.19.6">6</reference>).<div eID="gen22702" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22703" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">not enter into the city--</hi>as an enemy: as I entered Admah, Zeboim, and Sodom, utterly destroying them, whereas I will not utterly destroy thee. Somewhat similarly Jerome: "I am not one such as human dwellers in a city, who take cruel vengeance; I save those whom I correct." Thus "not man," and "in the midst of thee," are parallel to "into the city." Though I am in the midst of thee, it is not as man entering a rebellious city to destroy utterly. Maurer needlessly translates, "I will not come in wrath." <div eID="gen22703" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12393"/><div sID="gen22704" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12393"/><hi type="bold">10. he shall roar like a lion--</hi>by awful judgments on their foes (<reference osisRef="Isa.31.4">Is 31:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.25.26-Jer.25.30">Jr 25:26-30</reference>; <reference osisRef="Joel.3.16">Joe 3:16</reference>), calling His dispersed "children" from the various lands of their dispersion.<div eID="gen22704" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22705" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall tremble--</hi>shall flock in eager agitation of haste.<div eID="gen22705" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22706" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from the west--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Zech.8.7">Zec 8:7</reference>).
